reference.title: Cable Seated Curl
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read; the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you curl the bar up, breathe in as you lower it.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, short squeeze, 2-3 s down

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can curl without rocking the trunk back.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; slower lowering

cues.text: Sit tall on the end of a flat bench facing the low pulley, feet flat and a little wider than the hips. Hold the bar underhand about shoulder width, elbows a little in front of the ribs, bar just over the knees.
Breathe out and curl the bar toward the chest, moving only at the elbows.
Squeeze the biceps at the top; the elbows stay where they started and the trunk stays tall.
Breathe in and lower slowly until the bar is back over the knees, keeping the cable taut.

mistakes.mistake: Rocking the trunk back to start the curl
mistakes.fix: Sit tall with the feet planted; lighten the stack.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows drifting forward or flaring at the top
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arms still; stop when the forearms can go no higher without the elbows moving.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the bar drop onto the thighs
mistakes.fix: Lower over 2-3 s and stop with the bar just over the knees.
Keep the wrists straight in line with the forearms.

kinematics.norm: Full range: mean elbow range was about 117-123 degrees across barbell, EZ-bar and alternating dumbbell curls (Marcolin 2018)
Upper arms still, a little forward of the trunk so the bar clears the thighs at the bottom (clinical opinion)
Underhand (supinated) grip about shoulder width; the supinated grip gave the highest biceps activity in the lifting phase (Coratella 2023)
Sitting tall, feet flat, knees about 90 degrees; the seat removes leg drive and trunk sway (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion); biceps activity was lower while lowering than lifting at the same load (Oliveira 2009)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain in the elbow or shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with the trunk still.
Sit far enough from the pulley that the bar does not drag the hands into the thighs at the bottom.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Wrist discomfort with the straight bar: use an EZ-bar attachment or a rope.
Elbow pain at the bottom: stop a little short of the lowest position (clinical opinion).

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Prime mover: bends the elbow against the cable with the palm up. The seat and the still upper arms leave the elbow flexors to do the lift.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Prime mover: bends the elbow against the cable with the palm up. The seat and the still upper arms leave the elbow flexors to do the lift.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the bar and help bend the elbow.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the bar and help bend the elbow.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk tall on the bench so the bar is not rocked up.

guides.label: Elbows fully bent at the top
